11867-the-alaskan.title: The Alaskan
11867-the-alaskan.creator: James Oliver Curwood
11867-the-alaskan.description: A book by James Oliver Curwood. her wild call to those who had courage to come and fight for her treasures, and live—or die. Tonight, with the softly musical throb of his ship under his feet, and the yellow moon climbing up from behind the ramparts of the Alaskan mountains, something of loneliness seized upon him, and he said simply:  “That is Alaska.”  The girl standing beside him at the rail did not turn, nor for a moment did she answer.

arxiv-2012-00923.title: Nuanced and Interrelated Mediations and Exigencies (NIME): Addressing the Prevailing Political and Epistemological Crises Conference: NIME’20, July 21-25, 2020, Royal Birmingham Conservatoire, Birmingham City University, Birmingham, United Kingdom.
arxiv-2012-00923.creator: Lauren Hayes Adnan Marquez-Borbon
arxiv-2012-00923.description: Abstract Nearly two decades after its inception as a workshop at the ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, NIME exists as an established international conference significantly distinct from its precursor. While this origin story is often noted, the implications of NIME’s history as emerging from a field predominantly dealing with human-computer interaction have rarely been discussed.

arxiv-2104-06741.title: Diophantine problems over ℤ a ​ b \mathbb{Z}^{ab} modulo prime numbers
arxiv-2104-06741.creator: Konstantinos Kartas
arxiv-2104-06741.description: Abstract . Let ℤ a ​ b \mathbb{Z}^{ab} be the ring of integers of ℚ a ​ b \mathbb{Q}^{ab} , the maximal abelian extension of ℚ \mathbb{Q} . We show that there exists an algorithm to decide whether a system of equations and inequations, with integer coefficients, has a solution in ℤ a ​ b \mathbb{Z}^{ab} modulo every rational prime.

arxiv-2105-14839.title: Greedy-layer Pruning: Speeding up Transformer Models for Natural Language Processing Accepted at Pattern Recognition Letters ( https://www.journals.elsevier.com/pattern-recognition-letters )
arxiv-2105-14839.creator: David Peer, Sebastian Stabinger, Stefan Engl, Antonio Rodríguez-Sánchez
arxiv-2105-14839.description: Abstract Fine-tuning transformer models after unsupervised pre-training reaches a very high performance on many different natural language processing tasks. Unfortunately, transformers suffer from long inference times which greatly increases costs in production. One possible solution is to use knowledge distillation, which solves this problem by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models.

arxiv-2108-05591.title: Top degree Ext-groups and relatively supercuspidal spectra
arxiv-2108-05591.creator: Li Cai, Yangyu Fan
arxiv-2108-05591.description: Abstract . Relatively supercuspidal representations are analogue of supercuspidal representations in the relative Langlands program. This work studies relatively supercuspidal representations using top degree Ext-groups via the Schneider-Stuhler duality. As examples, the relatively supercuspidal spectra for the Flicker-Rallis case and the diagonal case are determined. 1. Introduction Let F be a p -adic field.

arxiv-2204-03774.title: Taking models seriously and being a linguistic realist
arxiv-2204-03774.creator: Raoni Wohnrath Arroyo
arxiv-2204-03774.description: Abstract \DeclareDelimFormat finalnamedelim & Abstract. Carnap’s conception of linguistic frameworks is widespread; however, it is not entirely clear nor consensual to pinpoint what is the influence in his stance within the traditional realist/anti-realist debate. In this paper, we place Carnap as a proponent of a scientific realist stance, by presenting what he called “linguistic realism”.

arxiv-2304-03854.title: Revisiting Deep Learning for Variable Type Recovery
arxiv-2304-03854.creator: Kevin Cao, Kevin Leach
arxiv-2304-03854.description: Abstract Compiled binary executables are often the only available artifact in reverse engineering, malware analysis, and software systems maintenance. Unfortunately, the lack of semantic information like variable types makes comprehending binaries difficult. In efforts to improve the comprehensibility of binaries, researchers have recently used machine learning techniques to predict semantic information contained in the original source code. Chen et al.

arxiv-2308-13828.title: Gaia view of primitive inner-belt asteroid families
arxiv-2308-13828.creator: M. Delbo, C. Avdellidou, K. J. Walsh
arxiv-2308-13828.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M. Delbo, C. Avdellidou, K. J. Walsh. Near-Earth asteroids Ryugu and Bennu, were visited, characterised, and sampled by the Hayabusa2 and OSIRIS-REx missions, where remote sensing data and sample return analysis showed that both asteroids have primitive, hydrated and organic-rich compositions. The dark families of the inner main belt that belong to the spectroscopic C-complex have been claimed to be the sources of both Ryugu and Bennu, hence there have been large efforts to spectroscopically characterise them by ground-based observations.

arxiv-2312-09893.title: Dynamical Casimir cooling in circuit QED systems
arxiv-2312-09893.creator: Sadeq S. Kadijani, Nicolás Del Grosso, Thomas L. Schmidt, M. Belén Farias
arxiv-2312-09893.description: Abstract A transmission line coupled to an externally driven superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) can exhibit the Dynamical Casimir Effect (DCE). Employing this setup, we quantize the SQUID degrees of freedom and show that it gives rise to a three-body interaction Hamiltonian with the cavity modes.

arxiv-2401-10346.title: Solution uniqueness of convex optimization problems via the radial cone
arxiv-2401-10346.creator: Jalal Fadili, Tran T. A. Nghia, Duy Nhat Phan
arxiv-2401-10346.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we mainly study solution uniqueness of some convex optimization problems. Our characterizations of solution uniqueness are in terms of the radial cone. This approach allows us to know when a unique solution is a strong solution or even a tilt-stable one without checking second-order information. Consequently, we apply our theory to low-rank optimization problems.

arxiv-2602-05204.title: Extreme Weather Nowcasting via Local Precipitation Pattern Prediction
arxiv-2602-05204.creator: Changhoon Song & Teng-Yuan Chang, Youngjoon Hong
arxiv-2602-05204.description: Abstract Accurate forecasting of extreme weather events such as heavy rainfall or storms is critical for risk management and disaster mitigation. Although high-resolution radar observations have spurred extensive research on nowcasting models, precipitation nowcasting remains particularly challenging due to pronounced spatial locality, intricate fine-scale rainfall structures, and variability in forecasting horizons.

pmc-10712722.title: In vitro activity of tebipenem and comparator agents against bacterial pathogens isolated from patients with cancer
pmc-10712722.creator: Bahgat Gerges, Joel Rosenblatt, Samuel A Shellburne, Anne-Marie Chaftari, Ray Hachem, Issam Raad
pmc-10712722.description: BackgroundTebipenem is a broad-spectrum orally administered carbapenem antibiotic that could be an alternative to IV carbapenems. The current study evaluated in vitro activity of tebipenem against bacterial isolates recovered from patients with cancer.MethodsA total of 611 bacterial pathogens recently isolated from patients with cancer were tested for susceptibility to tebipenem and comparators. CLSI-approved broth microdilution methods were used.

pmc-11557726.title: Evaluation of drug–drug interactions of a novel potent FLT3 inhibitor SKLB1028 in healthy subjects
pmc-11557726.creator: Jingcheng Chen, Jingxuan Wu, Nini Guo, Yuqin Song, Lijun Li, Bingyan Wang, Jiangshuo Li, Mengyu Hou, Hang Yin, Meijuan Zhang, Yanhong Kong, Xiaofang Wu, Ran Li, Le Wu, Qiannan Gao, Ruihua Dong
pmc-11557726.description: SKLB1028 is a novel multi‐target protein kinase inhibitor under investigation for the treatment of FLT3‐ITD mutated acute myeloid leukemia. Based on the preclinical characterization of SKLB1028 metabolism, three drug–drug interaction clinical studies were performed to investigate the effects of itraconazole, rifampin (CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, respectively), and gemfibrozil (CYP2C8 inhibitor) on the metabolism of SKLB1028.

pmc-11653554.title: Enhanced forecasting of emergency department patient arrivals using feature engineering approach and machine learning
pmc-11653554.creator: Bruno Matos Porto, Flavio Sanson Fogliatto
pmc-11653554.description: BackgroundEmergency department (ED) overcrowding is an important problem in many countries. Accurate predictions of ED patient arrivals can help management to better allocate staff and medical resources. In this study, we investigate the use of calendar and meteorological predictors, as well as feature-engineered variables, to predict daily patient arrivals using datasets from eleven different EDs across three countries.

pmc-12542244.title: Exploring the perspectives of young adults on mental healthcare and systemic health, education, and social challenges in Australia: a qualitative study
pmc-12542244.creator: Zahra Cooper, Bradley Roberts, Georgia Landery, Sarah Woodland, Khan R L Collins, Bernadette T Majda, Susanne Stanley, Anthony Akkari, Sean D Hood, Jennifer Rodger
pmc-12542244.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundYoung people often face significant challenges accessing effective mental health support as they navigate through complex healthcare systems, education pathways, and social pressures. Understanding the service-level barriers they encounter is critical to improving mental health system design and delivery.

pmc-13240840.title: Targeting NF-κB signaling for HIV latency reversal: Mechanisms, challenges, and therapeutic perspectives
pmc-13240840.creator: Maryam Mashhadi Abolghasem Shirazi, Seyed Mehdi Sadat
pmc-13240840.description: Highlights•NF-κB plays a dual role in HIV biology, functioning as both a key activator of viral transcription and a regulator of HIV latency maintenance.•Targeting NF-κB for HIV latency reversal is mechanistically attractive but therapeutically complex, due to risks of systemic inflammation and off-target gene activation.

pmc-13413701.title: The Impact of Time-to-Intervention on Mortality and Functional Outcome in Acute Subdural Hematoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13413701.creator: Bogdan Jabłoński, Wojciech Górecki, Justyna Fercho, Jacek Szypenbejl, Maksymilian Niemczyk, Oskar Chasles, Zuzanna Krasula, Zuzanna Wites, Mariusz Siemiński
pmc-13413701.description: Introduction: Acute subdural hematoma (aSDH) represents one of the most lethal and debilitating forms of traumatic brain injury (TBI) encountered in neurosurgical emergency settings, carrying high mortality rates and severe long-term functional deficits. Historically, the timing of surgical decompression has been considered a critical modifiable prognostic factor.
